articles.title: Gabriel García Márquez, Premio Nobel de Literatura: "Lo único que me duele de morir es que no sea de amor"
articles.standfirst: La soledad, un sentimiento cada vez más común en la era digital, puede motivarnos a buscar conexiones auténticas, tal como Gabriel García Márquez exploró en sus obras sobre la condición humana.
articles.summary: La soledad, un sentimiento cada vez más común en la era digital, puede motivarnos a buscar conexiones auténticas, tal como Gabriel García Márquez exploró en sus obras sobre la condición humana.
articles.body: El legado de Gabriel García Márquez, reflejado en su obra El amor en los tiempos del cólera, resuena especialmente en un mundo donde la soledad y la comparación social son problemas cotidianos. La cita “Lo único que me duele de morir es que no sea de amor” sintetiza la esencia de personas que buscan conexión emocional en una era marcada por la hiperconectividad. La creciente presión por ser productivos y la velocidad del día a día crean un contexto donde es fácil sentirse atrapado y sin dirección. La profundidad del individualismo se intensifica al lidiar con el vertiginoso ritmo de la vida moderna. En su obra, García Márquez plantea preguntas sobre la identidad y la búsqueda de propósito en medio de la deshumanización provocada por el consumismo. En un momento en que la incertidumbre prevalece, la literatura del autor ofrece una reflexión sobre la lucha inherente entre el amor y la soledad, un desafío que resuena hoy más que nunca. Para comprender el sentimiento de soledad que muchos experimentan en la actualidad, el pensamiento de Gabriel García Márquez ofrece una perspectiva especialmente interesante. Su reflexión sobre el tema de la soledad plantea que esta condición es tanto una experiencia personal como una realidad humana universal, esculpida a través de sus narrativas donde los personajes a menudo enfrentan la desconexión emocional, lo cual resuena con el fenómeno de la soledad en la era digital. Gabriel García Márquez, escritor colombiano nacido en 1927, se convirtió en una de las figuras más prominentes del boom latinoamericano y del realismo mágico. Su obra más reconocida, "Cien años de soledad", ha resonado en todo el mundo, siendo un hito literario que refleja las dimensiones de la cultura y conflictos latinoamericanos. Con su estilo único, García Márquez fusiona lo fantástico con lo cotidiano, creando historias que exploran la vida humana desde una perspectiva rica y compleja. Su capacidad para abordar temas como el amor y la soledad lo ha consagrado como un autor de referencia, destacando frases memorables como: “Lo único que me duele de morir es que no sea de amor”. El pensamiento de García Márquez está marcado por la dualidad entre lo real y lo fantástico. Su uso del realismo mágico permite una narrativa donde lo cotidiano se entrelaza con lo sobrenatural, ofreciendo una nueva forma de comprender la realidad. En sus obras, la soledad se presenta no solo como un sentimiento individual, sino como un reflejo de una condición humana universal que trasciende fronteras. Así, se puede relacionar su visión con autores como Julio Cortázar, quien también explora estructuras narrativas innovadoras que desafían la lógica tradicional. Esta conexión entre sus ideas y las de otros autores del boom latinoamericano revela una profunda reflexión sobre la identidad cultural y la memoria en el continente.

articles.title: MORNING GLORY: 'Blue Blight' is spreading fast and only voters can stop it
articles.summary: Manufacturing jobs, gas prices, and college enrollment are declining in blue states as "blue blight" spreads, reshaping where students choose to live.
articles.body: "Blue blight" is spreading across northeastern and west coast America, with scattered outbreaks in the interior of the country like Illinois and Colorado. It is up to voters to stop its spread. "Blue blight" isn’t a term-of-art yet. But, it will be. Consider that Dutch Elm Disease wasn’t a term familiar to Americans in the 1920s either. The devastating fungus arrived in the United States in the early 1930s, and notably impacted a handful of Elm trees in Cleveland, Ohio. By the end of the 1970s, the Elms that had defined the Courthouse Square of my hometown of Warren as well as my own street, and, indeed, all of northeast Ohio were almost all gone. The fungus spread far and wide beyond Ohio, leaving a trail of felled tree stumps in its wake. To this day it remains a threat to the remaining Elm population in the United States, even after it killed 3 out of 4 Elms across the country, and almost all of them in some places like northeastern Ohio. CALIFORNIA CONTROLLER CANDIDATE SLAMS MASSIVE EDUCATION SPENDING DESPITE WORSE STUDENT RESULTS The impacts of "blue blight" are becoming as visible as that of Dutch Elm Disease. Those impacts are most noticeable, to cite just two examples, in decreases in the quality of public education and declines in manufacturing jobs, even as state and local taxes rise. The second order impacts are now being felt across universities and colleges in states that are considered "blue." Kudos to the Wall Street Journal’s Douglas Belkin and Roshan Fernandez for their August 29 article titled "Why Syracuse Can’t Attract the Students It Needs to Pay the Bills." Kudos as well to Mary Katharine Ham and Vic Matus of the "Getting Hammered" podcast for some interesting speculation, prompted by the work of Belkin and Fernandez, on how the smaller number of college students — just the demographics of the decade ahead — are going to be looking beyond their choice of college to the job market and cost-of-living in the area surrounding their future campus and factoring those variables into their enrollment decision. Ham and Matus commented that perhaps students are going to tilt south to states like Florida rather than north to New York if they are looking at life choices ahead. Life choices as in "here are the jobs" and "what’s it cost to live in that state long term?" THE REAL REASON AMERICANS ARE FLEEING BLUE STATES FOR FLORIDA AND TEXAS I checked the numbers that are available against their thesis and, indeed, the available stats back them up. Using the data available from the Department of Education’s National Center for Education Statistics for the years 2017-2022 (the latest available) "blue states" — those that voted for then Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 — experienced substantially faster enrollment decline in higher ed than red states. NEW YORK CITY'S DECLINING PUBLIC SCHOOL ENROLLMENT PROJECTED TO LOSE OVER 150K MORE AS POPULATION DECLINES Of the six states that saw enrollments rise in their colleges and universities, five are "red": Georgia, Kentucky, Arizona, Indiana and Utah. Some deep red states did poorly (Alaska and Iowa) but the overall trend is there. Another factor to check on: manufacturing jobs. CEO SAYS DOING BUSINESS IN STATE ‘SUCKS’ AS COMPANY HEADS TO TEXAS AMID CALIFORNIA EXODUS When I first moved to California in 1978, its population was about 22 million souls and the state was home to close to 2 million manufacturing jobs. The Golden State’s population is today a half million shy of 40 million, but its total of manufacturing jobs has not simply failed to keep up with the population growth, the number of manufacturing jobs has actually plummeted to 1.2 million. Over 40 years the refining output in the state has dropped by a million barrels a day. California motorists are paying about far more per gallon than red state residents. The cost in Indiana is several dollars a gallon cheaper. "Blue blight" claims victims in many ways but nowhere more than among those who consume energy. No doubt some citizens prefer the blue abyss ahead for high tax/high regulation states. But all voters get to choose. And they get to change their minds if the spread of "blue blight" alarms them. articles.title: Un informe de la Guardia Civil confirma que la causa del accidente ferroviario de Adamuz fue causado por una rotura de la soldadura
articles.standfirst: El texto apunta a un deterioro previo al suceso
articles.summary: El texto apunta a un deterioro previo al suceso
articles.body: Tras casi nueve meses desde el trágico accidente ferroviario en Adamuz (Córdoba), el Informe Técnico de Inspección Ocular del Departamento de Escena del Crimen de la Guardia Civil confirma que la causa del suceso fue la rotura de la soldadura, que presentaba cierto deterioro previo al descarrilamiento y posterior choque entre los trenes Alvia e Iryo que acabó con la vida de 46 personas. El texto fue entregado al Juzgado de Montoro el pasado 3 de agosto y en él se señala al estado del acero de la vía de alta velocidad en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. A la altura del punto kilométrico 318+681 de la vía 1, la unión soldada tenía severas diferencias: un tramo de 1989 y otro más moderno de la marca Ensidesa 23. Según el informe, la soldadura se rompió y, al hacerlo, la barra más nueva se soltó y se movió hacia el exterior de la vía. El carril, además, no se quebró al paso del convoy, sino que ya arrastraba mucho deterioro previamente y la Guardia Civil detectó una mancha en forma de grajo sobre la zona donde la barra se ensancha y asienta sobre la traviesa. Los expertos consideran probado que el material llevaba un período considerable mostrando signos de fatiga y todo acabó rompiéndose y provocando el accidente de Adamuz. El tren Alvia fue el que recibió el mayor impacto lateral: su primer coche se empotró contra el talud a 14 metros de los raíles y el segundo se partió por la mitad. Mientras tanto, el tren Iryo, que era el que circulaba por la vía rota, llegó a tirar 10 postes de la catenaria hasta detenerse 450 metros después. Uno de sus carros de ruedas salió despedido, mientras que los restantes permanecieron, aunque se detectaron cortes en forma de medialuna que se relacionan con los cortes provocados por el filo de la vía rota.

articles.title: Penn State fraternity cocaine deals grew to kilo loads as pledges helped package drugs, witnesses testify
articles.summary: A former Delta Upsilon member testified he bought kilogram loads of cocaine from an alleged top supplier and sold drugs to Penn State fraternity members.
articles.body: BELLEFONTE, Pa. – A former Penn State fraternity member testified Wednesday that he bought and sold cocaine in quantities that grew from 100 grams to 1-kilogram loads as prosecutors detailed allegations of a drug operation running through fraternities near campus. The testimony came during preliminary hearings at the Centre County Courthouse in Bellefonte, Pennsylvania, for Agostino Abbatiello, Mohammed Huraibi, Paul Robinson, Thomas Robinson and Robert Zanolla. The five defendants are among 14 people charged in the alleged Penn State drug operation. Charging documents filed by the Pennsylvania attorney general’s office describe a hierarchy of alleged suppliers, distributors and fraternity members accused of weighing, packaging and delivering cocaine. Prosecutors allege the drugs were brought to State College from Philadelphia, New York and Long Island before being sold to Penn State students. SUSPECT ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY RUNNING METH LAB AT MICHIGAN STATE UNIVERSITY’S LARGEST ACADEMIC BUILDING Thomas Robinson, a former Delta Upsilon fraternity member, testified that he and Huraibi began buying cocaine from Abbatiello in 2023. Robinson said their first purchase involved about 100 grams of cocaine for roughly $4,000. Robinson testified that he stored the cocaine in his fraternity room, where he and Huraibi broke it down into half-gram bags and sold each one for about $80. JEANINE PIRRO CALLS OUT 'DIRTBAGS' AFTER 14 CHARGED IN ALLEGED COCAINE RING OPERATING FEET FROM A SCHOOLYARD He described additional purchases involving 250 grams, 500 grams and, eventually, about 1 kilogram of cocaine. Robinson testified that he began buying directly from Abbatiello through Snapchat after Huraibi stopped selling. Robinson said the Snapchat messages disappeared after 24 hours. During one March 2024 transaction, he testified that Abbatiello sold him about 500 grams of cocaine for approximately $22,000. DOJ ANNOUNCES 81 ALLEGED GANG MEMBERS INDICTED AFTER PUERTO RICO DRUG TRAFFICKING TAKEDOWN Robinson also testified that he purchased about 1 kilogram of cocaine from Abbatiello in July 2024, another kilogram in September and a third kilogram in November. He said he sold the drugs primarily to members of Penn State fraternities. The complaints portray Abbatiello as a top-level supplier who allegedly used fraternity connections to distribute cocaine on campus. They also accuse him of supplying Robinson and other defendants. WATCH: Alleged Penn State drug ring leaders appear in court THREE COLLEGE FRATS IN CROSSHAIRS AS HAZING CLAIMS OF BOOZE, BURNS AND HOSPITAL TRIPS SPARK CRACKDOWN: SCHOOL The defense challenged Robinson’s credibility and memory, pointing out that he used cocaine while he was selling it. Robinson acknowledged that his drug use could have affected his recollection. He also testified that he was arrested in December 2024 and removed from the fraternity shortly afterward. Huraibi, another former Delta Upsilon member, testified that he and Robinson discussed buying cocaine in bulk to resell. Huraibi said they purchased 100 grams from Abbatiello for about $4,000 in August 2023 and 250 grams for approximately $10,000 in November. MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY Huraibi testified that he and Robinson initially packaged the cocaine themselves, but that fraternity pledges later helped. He said he stopped participating after pledges became involved. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X The complaints accuse other fraternity members of supporting the alleged operation by helping package, deliver or purchase cocaine. One complaint accuses Michael Brogno Jr. of packaging and delivering drugs at Robinson’s direction. Other defendants are accused of using a digital scale, assisting with deliveries or buying cocaine from the larger distributors. BORDER AGENTS UNCOVER $20M COCAINE STASH HIDDEN BENEATH TRUCK FLOORBOARDS IN MASSIVE BUST Lars Zeepvat, a former Sigma Chi member, testified that Abbatiello’s alleged drug sales grew out of personal cocaine use. Zeepvat said Abbatiello later shifted toward selling cocaine for money and popularity. Zeepvat also testified that Abbatiello sometimes kept cocaine in fraternity houses and apartments, where students gathered to use it. He described an alleged November 2024 delivery to Delta Upsilon involving a large brown bag that Abbatiello said contained about 400 grams of cocaine. $290M COCAINE HAUL FOUND ‘SKILLFULLY CONCEALED’ IN MASSIVE BANANA SHIPMENT The complaints also accuse Zeepvat and Zanolla of making trips to New York to obtain cocaine for Abbatiello. Zanolla allegedly helped transport the drugs back to the State College area. In a separate hearing Wednesday, Ryan Matson testified that Paul Robinson helped retrieve a safe that had been hidden in the woods after Thomas Robinson’s arrest. Matson said Thomas wanted to keep drugs and money from being discovered during a potential raid. He said Robinson later urged him not to tell anyone about the safe. Under questioning, Matson acknowledged that he never opened it and initially withheld information from investigators because he wanted to protect Thomas. articles.title: IIT Madras student ranks among top 0.6% in Google for Developers hackathon: Meet Shreyansh Gupta, the young developer building with AI and AR
articles.summary: News News: For many students, a hackathon is an opportunity to test their coding skills. For IIT Madras BS learner Shreyansh Gupta, it became a chance to demonst.
articles.body: For many students, a hackathon is an opportunity to test their coding skills. For IIT Madras BS learner Shreyansh Gupta, it became a chance to demonstrate how technology can be used to tackle a real-world problem. Shreyansh secured rank 278 among 46,719 participants, placing him in the top 0.6% at the Google for Developers × Hack2skill PromptWars 2026 hackathon.His performance was particularly notable for the scores awarded to his solution. Shreyansh recorded an AI Evaluation Score of 88.81 out of 100, with perfect marks for efficiency and near-perfect scores for problem-statement alignment and accessibility. His achievement comes alongside a growing portfolio spanning full-stack development, artificial intelligence, augmented reality and student-led technology initiatives.IIT Madras learner takes on a real-world challengeShreyansh participated in Challenge 1: Physical Event Experience, which focused on improving the experience of people attending large-scale sporting venues.The challenge involved addressing practical problems such as crowd movement, waiting times and real-time coordination. Instead of treating the problem purely as a coding exercise, participants were expected to design solutions that could work in complex, real-world environments.Shreyansh's submission received 100/100 for efficiency, 98/100 for problem-statement alignment, 98/100 for accessibility and 96/100 for security.The overall evaluation considered factors including code quality, security, efficiency, testing, accessibility and how closely the proposed solution addressed the challenge.For Shreyansh, the experience reflects a broader approach to technology: learning concepts and then turning them into usable products.“Every challenge is an opportunity to turn what you learn into something that can solve a real problem.”From IIT Madras to AI agent developmentShreyansh is currently pursuing a BS in Data Processing at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, with his programme listed as running from 2025 to 2029.Alongside his studies, he is working as an AI Agent Developer Intern at TripXplo, a product of Tripmilestone Tours Pvt. Ltd. His work involves developing autonomous AI agents for travel-planning tasks.His responsibilities include building agent workflows using LangChain, integrating OpenAI and Claude APIs, developing memory and context-aware systems, and working on AI-driven automation for trip planning, booking assistance and customer queries.This experience places him at the intersection of software development and the rapidly evolving field of agentic AI.He is also building in ARAI is not Shreyansh's only area of interest.Since November 2025, he has also been working as a Snapchat Lens Creator, developing interactive augmented-reality lenses using Snap Lens Studio.His work includes face filters, world lenses and interactive effects involving 3D objects, animations, scripts and visual effects. The experience has given him hands-on exposure to AR, 3D design and user interaction.His LinkedIn profile describes his core identity simply: a builder.His technology journey extends beyond codingShreyansh has also taken up technical and leadership roles within student communities.He is currently a Technical Department Volunteer at Paradox, IIT Madras, contributing to the planning, development and execution of technical events. He is also part of the Technical Team at Boundless – IITM BS Travel Society, where he works on digital platforms, web applications and technical solutions for the IIT Madras BS community.Earlier, he served as a Campus Ambassador for Tryst 2026 at IIT Delhi and TATVA Fest 2026 at IIT Bombay. He also worked with the Entrepreneurship Development Cell at IIT Delhi, where he supported outreach, promotion and student engagement initiatives.These roles have added another dimension to his technical profile: working with teams, communicating ideas and building technology for communities rather than working only on individual projects.Building skills across AI, web development and entrepreneurshipBefore his current AI-focused internship, Shreyansh worked as a web developer and has experience with React and Firebase, including full-stack applications with authentication, real-time databases and administrative dashboards.He has also explored entrepreneurship and is involved in co-building a direct-to-consumer clothing brand, KREVVA.His academic and technical exposure extends beyond IIT Madras as well. In 2025, he completed an intensive certificate course at IIT-BHU on sustainable infrastructure monitoring with AI-inspired machine learning under the GIAN initiative. The course covered areas including machine learning algorithms, data preprocessing, neural networks, predictive maintenance and anomaly detection.More than a hackathon rankShreyansh's PromptWars result stands out because it brings together several strands of his journey: formal learning at IIT Madras, hands-on software development, AI-agent experimentation, AR creation and participation in technology communities.The rank of 278 out of 46,719 participants is one measurable outcome. But the larger story is how a student is using opportunities across different technology domains to move from learning concepts to building systems designed for actual users.For students looking at careers in AI and software development, his journey also highlights an increasingly important lesson: coding skills become more valuable when they are combined with problem-solving, experimentation and the ability to build something that works beyond the classroom.Disclaimer: This article is based on publicly available information and professional details shared in Shreyansh Gupta's profile and the hackathon-related information provided for this article.
